i1_governing_problem_and_scale: The compliance of providers of general-purpose AI models with the Chapter V obligations is supervised, evaluated and sanctioned at Union level; scope: general-purpose AI models placed on the Union market, Union jurisdiction, from the Chapter V application date (2 August 2025, Article 113)
i2_coupling_description: Qualified conditional dependencies: classification (Articles 51-52) conditions the Article 55 obligations; reliance on codes of practice or demonstration of alternative means is assessed by the Commission (Articles 53(4), 55(2)); fines under Article 101 are conditioned on non-compliance with requests, measures and access requests under Articles 91 to 93; scientific panel alerts trigger the Commission powers (Articles 52(4), 90); the Board is informed or consulted (Articles 90(2), 92(1), 101(4)); fines are reviewed by the Court of Justice (Article 101(5))
i3_configurational_consequence: A closed enforcement path at Union level: from classification to obligations, monitoring and evaluation, requests and measures, fines and judicial review, with the same authority at every step; accountability interface between providers and the Commission with external judicial review
i3_bearer_and_rule: Bearer ARCHITECTURE arch_gpai; rule: the Article 101(1) conditions refer to the Article 91-93 powers, so the sanction stage is legally coupled to the monitoring and evaluation stages; the property is not inferred from reachability
i4_evidence_searched: CL-01, CL-02 and CL-03: all units read; absence of national competence over Chapter V searched within the declared corpus
i4_rival_grouping: Treat the Commission powers over general-purpose AI models as part of a single market surveillance architecture through Article 75, or treat the codes of practice as a separate architecture
i4_boundary_sensitivity: If Article 75 is treated as a coupling to national market surveillance the candidate overlaps with the enforcement candidate; if the scientific panel (conditional on a further act) is excluded the alert coupling falls away but the monitoring-to-sanction coupling remains
outcome_basis: All four conditions are stated and evidenced for the single governance question; the I2 coupling is stated by explicit conditions in Articles 101 and 53 and does not rest on a common actor alone (the Commission); the outcome is provisional and queued
status_profile: Constituent relations: legal_constitution_evidenced except those depending on the scientific panel (conditional_on_further_act, documented) and the alternative-means demonstration relations conditioned on harmonised standards (documented); 0 material_establishment_evidenced; 0 exercise_evidenced

i1_governing_problem_and_scale: Establishing conformity of high-risk AI systems with the Section 2 requirements before and during their placing on the market through operator verification, third-party certification by designated notified bodies and standards; scope: high-risk AI systems, Union internal market, from the Chapter III application dates
i2_coupling_description: Qualified procedural and conditional dependencies: importers and distributors verify the conformity assessment, CE marking and declaration (Articles 23(1), 24(1)); the provider route depends on the Annex III area and on the application of standards (Article 43); a conformity assessment body may act as notified body only after notification without objection (Article 30(4)); notified bodies issue and withdraw certificates under notifying authority supervision (Articles 36, 44); common specifications are conditioned on standardisation requests (Article 41)
i3_configurational_consequence: A two-route conformity path (internal control or notified body) whose outputs (certificate, CE marking, declaration) are verified downstream by importers and distributors and whose certifiers are designated and supervised by notifying authorities with Union objection and review
i3_bearer_and_rule: Bearer ARCHITECTURE arch_conf; rule: the downstream verification duties name the artifacts produced by the certification relations, and the certification relations are conditioned on notification outcomes, so the chain is coupled by legal conditions and not by reachability
i4_evidence_searched: CL-01, CL-02, CL-04 and CL-05: all units read; necessity of the notified body searched within the declared corpus
i4_rival_grouping: Treat operator verification duties, designation of notified bodies and certification as three separate architectures
i4_boundary_sensitivity: If the Annex I Section A route (external) were treated as part of the candidate the certification stage would be undetermined; excluding Annex I systems the candidate holds for the declared corpus
outcome_basis: The four conditions are stated for the governance question of conformity establishment; the coupling between operator verification and certification is a stated procedural dependency, not a shared actor; the standards coupling is weaker and the outcome is provisional and queued
status_profile: Constituent relations: legal_constitution_evidenced except relations and assignments conditioned on unresolved external references (documented); 0 material_establishment_evidenced; 0 exercise_evidenced; Annex I Section A route undetermined

i1_governing_problem_and_scale: Enforcement of the Regulation against AI systems placed on the market or in service through national market surveillance authorities with Union review of national measures, operator duties towards authorities, incident reporting and the supervision of Union bodies by the European Data Protection Supervisor; scope: AI systems, Member State and Union levels
i2_coupling_description: Qualified procedural linkages: incident and risk reports (Articles 20(2), 26(5), 73) are made to the market surveillance authorities that open the Article 79 procedure; provisional measures trigger notification and the Commission decision (Articles 79(5), 81); operators must demonstrate conformity on request (Articles 21, 22, 23, 24); for Union bodies the European Data Protection Supervisor replaces national authorities (Article 3(48))
i3_configurational_consequence: A two-level enforcement path in which an operator report or authority finding at national level can end in a Commission decision binding all Member States, with operators bound to supply documentation and cooperate at each step
i3_bearer_and_rule: Bearer ARCHITECTURE arch_enf; rule: Article 81(2) makes the Commission decision on a national measure binding on all Member States and Article 79(5) conditions the measure on inadequate corrective action after the evaluation, so the levels are coupled by explicit conditions
i4_evidence_searched: CL-01, CL-02, CL-06 and CL-07: all units read; absence of general direction powers searched within the declared corpus
i4_rival_grouping: Treat the Union safeguard procedure as a separate architecture from national measures, or merge enforcement with supervision of general-purpose AI models through Article 75
i4_boundary_sensitivity: The content of market surveillance powers is external (Regulation (EU) 2019/1020); the procedural chain of the candidate holds for the declared corpus; the alternative-path claim is undetermined (CL-07)
outcome_basis: The couplings are stated by explicit conditions and cross-references and name the authorities, the Commission and Member States; the external reference touches the content of powers, not the stated relations; the outcome is provisional and queued
status_profile: Constituent relations: legal_constitution_evidenced; 0 material_establishment_evidenced; 0 exercise_evidenced; the content of the market surveillance powers is undetermined

i1_governing_problem_and_scale: Adaptation of Annex content and thresholds by delegated acts adopted by the Commission under a delegation conferred and overseen by the European Parliament and the Council; scope: the twelve provisions listed in Article 97(2), Union jurisdiction, five years from 1 August 2024 tacitly renewable
i2_coupling_description: Cross-reference coupling: each competence names Article 97; the European Parliament and the Council confer, may revoke and may object (Article 97(2), (3), (6)); the Commission reports and notifies (Article 97(2), (5)) and consults Member State experts (Article 97(4))
i3_configurational_consequence: A bounded delegation: Commission competences across several Articles are subject to common conferral, revocation and objection controls
i3_bearer_and_rule: Bearer ARCHITECTURE arch_deleg; rule: Article 97(6) makes the entry into force of each delegated act conditional on the absence of objection, a property attributable to the whole delegation
i4_evidence_searched: CL-01 and CL-02: all units read; the competences listed in Article 97(2) were located
i4_rival_grouping: Treat each competence as an isolated Commission competence
i4_boundary_sensitivity: Implementing acts under Article 98(2) are excluded because their procedure rests on an external Regulation; including them would make the whole undetermined
outcome_basis: A single delegation article couples the competences by explicit cross-references and oversight relations; the candidate is small and the outcome is provisional and queued

i1_governing_problem_and_scale: Whether the delegated-act and implementing-act competences of the Commission form one rule-making architecture; scope: Commission competences citing Article 97 or Article 98(2)
i2_coupling_description: No coupling between the delegation relations (Article 97) and the committee relation (Article 98) is stated: they are separate procedures sharing the Commission as actor; the committee procedure rests on an external Regulation
i3_configurational_consequence: No property attributable to the whole could be stated without presupposing the coupling
i3_bearer_and_rule: Not stated: a shared actor and a shared procedural article would only re-describe the inventory
i4_evidence_searched: CL-01 and CL-02: all units read; the committee procedure content is not retrievable
i4_rival_grouping: Two distinct architectures (delegation; implementing acts) or one rule-making architecture
i4_boundary_sensitivity: A distinct-architectures claim requires sufficient coverage, which is lacking because the examination procedure is external and constitutive
outcome_basis: A DISTINGUISHABLE outcome would require sufficient declared coverage, and an INTEGRATED outcome would require a stated coupling that is absent; the committee procedure is an unresolved constitutive external reference (RGAM-DR-25)
status_profile: Constituent relations: delegation relations legal_constitution_evidenced; committee relation documented with constitutive dependency; 0 material_establishment_evidenced; 0 exercise_evidenced

i1_governing_problem_and_scale: Controlled experimentation with innovative AI systems through authority-supervised sandboxes and approved testing in real world conditions; scope: providers and prospective providers, Member State and Union levels, with the sandbox obligation operational by 2 August 2026
i2_coupling_description: Qualified procedural dependencies: sandbox participation follows a sandbox plan agreed with the competent authority (Article 57(5)); real-world testing requires market surveillance authority approval and may be suspended or terminated by it (Articles 60(4)(b), 76(3)); exit reports and written proof are taken into account by market surveillance authorities and notified bodies (Article 57(7)); reports go to the AI Office and the Board (Article 57(15)-(16))
i3_configurational_consequence: An authority-gated route to the market in which participation, approval, supervision, suspension and reporting are linked, with exit documentation feeding later conformity assessment and surveillance
i3_bearer_and_rule: Bearer ARCHITECTURE arch_sandbox; rule: the approval condition of Article 60(4)(b) and the suspension power of Article 76(3) bind testing to the authority decision
i4_evidence_searched: CL-01 and CL-02: all units read; Articles 57 to 62 and 76 located
i4_rival_grouping: Separate sandboxes (Articles 57-59) from real-world testing outside sandboxes (Articles 60-61, 76)
i4_boundary_sensitivity: If real-world testing outside sandboxes is excluded, the sandbox relations remain coupled; overlap with market surveillance and certification arises through Articles 57(7) and 76
outcome_basis: Stated couplings between participation, approval, supervision and reporting satisfy the four conditions for a single question; the outcome is provisional and queued

i1_governing_problem_and_scale: Coordination and advice among Union governance bodies and Member States for the consistent application of the Regulation; scope: Union level, Board, advisory forum, scientific panel, AI Office
i2_coupling_description: Mandatory consultation and advice interfaces between the Commission, the Board, the advisory forum and the scientific panel are stated, but the scientific panel depends on a further implementing act and the advisory forum norm type is ambiguous
i3_configurational_consequence: An advisory coordination layer with the Commission as secretariat and consulted party; the whole-level property cannot be stated without assuming the constitution of the panel and the forum
i3_bearer_and_rule: Bearer ARCHITECTURE arch_gov; rule not stated: the constitutive status of two members is undetermined
i4_evidence_searched: CL-01 and CL-02: all units read
i4_rival_grouping: Treat the Board, the advisory forum and the scientific panel as separate bodies each attached to the Commission
i4_boundary_sensitivity: The constitution of the scientific panel rests on an implementing act outside W and the AI Office on an external decision, so any whole-level claim is restricted to the declared corpus
outcome_basis: I3 and I4 are not satisfied: the whole-level property depends on elements whose legal constitution is conditional on further acts or external decisions
status_profile: Constituent relations: Board relations legal_constitution_evidenced; panel relations conditional_on_further_act (documented); forum relations with ambiguous norm type; 0 material_establishment_evidenced; 0 exercise_evidenced

i1_governing_problem_and_scale: Control of real-time and post-remote biometric identification by law enforcement through authorisation, notification and reporting; scope: law enforcement use, Member State and Union levels
i2_coupling_description: The authorisation, notification and reporting relations are chained by explicit cross-references (Article 5(3)-(7); Article 26(10)), but the real-time chain operates only where a Member State has provided for authorisation by national law (Article 5(5)) and the party requesting and notifying is identified only by cross-reference
i3_configurational_consequence: A layered authorisation, notification and reporting chain, conditional on national rules
i3_bearer_and_rule: Bearer ARCHITECTURE arch_rbi; rule stated for the chain but its existence depends on a Member State decision
i4_evidence_searched: CL-01 and CL-02: all units read
i4_boundary_sensitivity: Where no Member State adopts national rules the real-time authorisation chain does not operate; the claim is restricted to Member States that have decided under Article 5(5)
outcome_basis: The architecture is conditional on further national acts (legal status conditional_on_further_act of the chain relations) and counterpart identification rests on a cross-reference reading; the stopping rule limits the claim to the S level
status_profile: Constituent relations: authorisation, notification and reporting relations conditional_on_further_act (documented); 0 material_establishment_evidenced; 0 exercise_evidenced

i1_governing_problem_and_scale: Whether the Regulation as a whole constitutes one governance architecture for AI systems and general-purpose AI models in the Union; the purpose and the matters laid down are stated in Article 1(1)-(2) and the scope in Article 2
i2_coupling_description: Source-supported couplings between the candidate architectures: Article 75 (supervision of general-purpose AI models and market surveillance), Article 43(1) third subparagraph and Article 79(2) (market surveillance authority acting as notified body and informing notified bodies), Article 57(7) and Article 76 (sandboxes with certification and surveillance), Article 83 (formal non-compliance of artifacts of the conformity process), the shared EU database (Articles 49, 71, 80(8)) and Board consultations (Articles 6(5), 40(2), 71(1), 92(1)); no coupling covers all candidates
i3_configurational_consequence: Not attributable to the whole without presupposing the integration: any whole-level property (a single governance architecture of the instrument) would re-describe the inventory; per-candidate properties are stated at candidate level
i3_bearer_and_rule: Not stated: no inferential rule links the candidate properties into a property of the whole
i4_evidence_searched: CL-01 and CL-02: all units read; coupling provisions between candidates located
i4_rival_grouping: Treat the candidates as distinct architectures coupled only through shared actors (Commission, market surveillance authorities, providers), or as one instrument-wide architecture
i4_boundary_sensitivity: Treating the overlaps as couplings gives partial integration; treating them as incidental cross-references gives distinguishable candidates; the external references limit both readings
outcome_basis: The candidates are coupled at source-supported points but no stated coupling or whole-level property covers them all; the intersections are not treated as a new architecture; the shared actors alone do not warrant integration
status_profile: Constituent relations: legal_constitution_evidenced for most; documented or undetermined where conditional on further acts or external dependency; 0 material_establishment_evidenced; 0 exercise_evidenced
